title: Butternut & silken tofu soup
summary: Silky squash soup with silken tofu blended in for protein you can't taste.
ingredients: 600g butternut squash, peeled, deseeded and cubed
Squeeze of lemon, and salt to taste
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the squash and stock and simmer for 20 minutes until very soft.
Add the tofu and nutmeg and blend until completely smooth.
Finish with lemon and salt.
tip: Silken tofu adds protein to a gentle soup without changing the texture.
swaps: Use peeled sweet potato instead of squash

storage.text: Fridge for 3 days or freeze in portions for 3 months. Blend again after thawing if it separates.

title: Cheesy egg-enriched mash
summary: Extra-smooth mash with egg yolk and cheese beaten in — soft, filling and nourishing.
ingredients: 500g floury potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
steps: Boil the potatoes for 15 minutes until very soft. Drain well.
Mash until completely smooth, or push through a sieve.
Over a low heat, beat in the butter, milk, egg yolks and cheese for 2 minutes until glossy and hot.
Season and serve.
tip: Beating the yolks into hot mash cooks them through and adds protein and energy when appetite is low.
swaps: Use oat milk and olive oil for a dairy-free version, and leave out the cheese

storage.text: Fridge for 2 days. Freezes for 1 month but may go a little grainy — beat in a splash of milk when reheating until piping hot.

title: Vanilla protein shake
summary: A creamy, energy-rich shake made from everyday ingredients — no protein powder needed.
steps: Blend everything until smooth and frothy.
Drink chilled, slowly.
tip: Milk powder roughly doubles the protein of a glass of milk without making it bigger.
swaps: Add ½ ripe banana for a thicker shake

storage.text: Best fresh. Keeps 1 day in a sealed bottle in the fridge — shake well.

title: Smooth herby cottage cheese dip
summary: A no-cook, high-protein dip blended until silky, with soft warm pitta.
ingredients: 1 tbsp very finely chopped dill or chives
1 lemon, zested, plus a squeeze of juice
steps: Blend the cottage cheese and oil until completely smooth.
Stir in the herbs, lemon zest and juice. Season.
Serve with warm pitta, cut into strips.
tip: Blending removes the curds for a smooth texture. Leave out the herbs on harder days.
swaps: Use ricotta instead of cottage cheese

storage.text: Keep covered in the fridge for 3 days. Don't freeze.

title: Yoghurt & seedless jam pot
summary: A no-cook snack in two minutes — thick yoghurt swirled with smooth jam.
steps: Spoon the yoghurt into a bowl or jar.
Swirl through the jam and honey.
tip: Check the jam says seedless — raspberry and strawberry jams usually have seeds.
swaps: Use stewed pear or apple instead of jam

storage.text: Best made fresh. Can be made the night before and kept covered in the fridge.

title: Peanut butter & banana toast
summary: A quick, filling snack — smooth peanut butter and mashed banana on soft white toast.
steps: Toast the bread lightly.
Spread with peanut butter.
Mash the banana on top and sprinkle with cinnamon.
tip: Lightly toasted white bread is softer than very crisp toast. Use smooth nut butter only.
swaps: Use smooth tahini instead of peanut butter

title: Poached eggs on buttery mash
summary: A light, gentle supper — soft poached eggs on smooth mash with a little chive butter.
ingredients: 500g potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
steps: Boil the potatoes for 15 minutes until very soft. Drain and mash smooth with the butter and milk.
Bring a pan of water to a gentle simmer and poach the eggs for 3 minutes.
Spoon the mash on to plates, top with the eggs and scatter over the chives.
tip: Lower in fat than most comfort food, and soft all the way through.

storage.text: Best eaten straight away. Leftover mash keeps 2 days in the fridge — cook eggs fresh.

title: Soft couscous with roast squash
summary: Fluffy lemon couscous with tender roast squash and crumbled feta. Light and quick.
ingredients: 300g butternut squash, peeled and cut into small cubes
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the squash with the oil and cumin and roast for 25 minutes until very soft.
Pour the hot stock over the couscous, cover and leave for 10 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and stir in the lemon zest and juice.
Top with the squash, feta and parsley.
tip: Couscous is made from refined wheat and is soft and quick. Use the finest you can find.
swaps: Use paneer or halloumi instead of feta
Use white rice instead of couscous

storage.text: Fridge for 2 days. Eat cold or reheat until piping hot. Don't freeze.

title: Potato & cheese pierogi
summary: Polish dumplings filled with cheesy mash, served with soft buttery onions and soured cream.
ingredients: 300g plain flour, plus extra for rolling
steps: Mix the flour, egg, water and oil into a soft dough. Knead for 5 minutes, cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Boil the potatoes until very soft, then mash smooth with the cottage cheese and cheddar. Season and cool.
Cook the onions in the butter over a low heat for 25 minutes until very soft and golden.
Roll the dough thinly, cut 8cm circles, add a spoonful of filling and pinch the edges closed.
Cook in simmering salted water for 3–4 minutes after they float.
Toss in the onions and butter, and serve with soured cream.
tip: Cook the onions low and slow until they're very soft. Chew the dumpling edges well.
swaps: Leave out the onions and use melted butter with a little dill

storage.text: Freeze uncooked pierogi on a tray, then bag for 3 months — boil from frozen for 6–7 minutes. Cooked pierogi keep 2 days in the fridge.

title: Pumpkin & tofu coconut curry
summary: A fragrant Thai-style curry without curry paste or chilli — lemongrass, lime and ginger do the work.
ingredients: 500g pumpkin or butternut squash, peeled and cubed
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes, then add the ginger for 1 minute.
Add the lemongrass, pumpkin, coconut milk, stock, soy and sugar. Simmer for 15–20 minutes until the pumpkin is very soft.
Remove the lemongrass. Add the tofu and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the lime juice and serve with rice.
tip: Lemongrass is too fibrous to eat, so it's always removed before serving. Most Thai curry pastes contain chilli and shrimp, so this doesn't use one.
swaps: Use light coconut milk for a lighter curry

storage.text: Fridge for 3 days or freeze for 3 months. Cook rice fresh, or cool leftover rice within 1 hour, fridge, and eat within 1 day; reheat only once.
